messages.subject: cannot get png looking correctly
parts:
Hi Group,

I have some code below. I am trying to get the plot as a png. If I use

ggsave(file = "myoutput.pdf"), things look great. But doing this with
png makes the
text small and the quality does not appear to be good either. I've tried various
combinations of height, width, and dpi, but it has not worked out so
far. Any suggestions?
Thanks for your time.

Regards,

Juliet

0.0170 0.8000 996
0.0170 0.9000 1219
0.021 0.7 686
0.021 0.8 805
0.021 0.9 985"),header=FALSE)
closeAllConnections();
colnames(myData) <- c("Effect","Power","N")
p <- ggplot(data=myData,aes(x=Effect,y=N))
p <- p+geom_point(aes(shape=factor(Power))) +
geom_line(aes(group=factor(Power)))
p <- p+scale_x_continuous(expression("Effect Size as "*R^2))
p <- p + scale_shape(name="Power")

R-help, where some of the windows graphics experts might be able to
help you.

messages.author: c304bceb5498cb4b
messages.subject: Re: cannot get png looking correctly
parts:
Hi Juliet,

I had similar issue as well and i tried all the rendering options
listed in the Hadley's book (great book!).
None of them turned out to be the same as PDF. I am not sure why but i
suspect that i have some
mistakes in my code which might be minor that ggplot2 can still
tolerate / interpret them. But when
it comes to save the plot into other standard rending format, it will
not be a flawless file. In my case,
my code was quite complicated. In the PNG file, the legend box takes
up the whole space while the
real plot was shrinked to non-discernable. And all the transparency
(alpha =0.4) was gone in the PNG
file. But the plot looks perfectly fine in the graphics window ...

Anyhow, a way to get around is that you can use R console menu to save
the plot instead of calling ggsave().
That worked for me. Hopefully this helps you.

Yongsheng

messages.author: 166e40180306ffff
messages.subject: Re: cannot get png looking correctly
parts:
Hello,

I also had big problems to generate correct looking png-files with
complicated figures. I finally gave up and used a not very elegant but
very efficient work around (only applicable for windows users). Just
save your figures as pdf-files. Install the freely available PDF-
XChange Viewer. It's much better than adobe reader anyway.
http://www.docu-track.com/home/prod_user/PDF-XChange_Tools/pdfx_viewer

Open the pdf-file in the XChange Viewer and save it in any format and
resolution you want (including png among others). I has always given
me perfect results so far.

Cheers,
Erich

messages.author: f5910785f085320f
messages.subject: Re: cannot get png looking correctly
parts:
I had a similar problem a while back using linux using png's.

After some head scratching, I noticed that a required font library
was missing. Installing the font library made the png files look as
intended. Not sure if that is helpful with respect to your png
problem, but I would look for things that may be missing under-the-
hood that would normally be expected to be present.

Avram
